one_line: Mughal emperor Akbar and Rajput general Raja Man Singh as allied architects and enforcers of the evolving mansabdari system.

appearance.age_look: Akbar early 30s, compact and athletic; Man Singh late 30s, taller and broad-shouldered, both robust and battle-hardened.
appearance.face: Akbar has an oval face, wheatish complexion, neatly trimmed pointed beard and thin mustache, keen almond eyes with a calm, evaluating gaze; Man Singh has a squarer jaw, slightly deeper complexion, full beard and thicker mustache, with intense, resolute eyes; both usually wear composed, serious expressions with a hint of mutual trust.
appearance.hair: Akbar’s hair is dark, straight, worn to the nape and hidden under a low, rounded Mughal turban in soft cream with a narrow emerald-green band and a single small white feather; Man Singh’s dark hair is tied in a tight warrior’s knot at the back of his head and wrapped with a bright saffron Rajput turban (pagri) with a modest gold brocade edge, no oversized plume.
appearance.costume: Akbar wears a long, calf-length Mughal jama crossing to the right in rich deep maroon silk with subtle golden floral bootis, fastened with small gold buttons and a narrow emerald sash at the waist, over slim off-white churidar trousers and soft brown leather mojari shoes; around his waist sits a plain, practical leather kamarband supporting a simple dagger sheath, and he wears minimal jewellery: a single jade ring and small gold stud earrings; Man Singh wears a knee-length, slightly flared cotton angarkha in muted indigo with a fine block-printed floral pattern, tied with fabric cords, over mail-and-plate armour visible as a fitted, dull-steel chest vest with small brass rivets, a broad dark-red cloth patka sash at his waist, mustard-yellow churidar trousers, and sturdy brown leather riding boots; his forearms are covered with simple leather bracers, and he wears a modest gold stud earring in each ear and a small tilak mark on his forehead, both men fully and modestly clothed with all torsos and legs covered.
appearance.signature: Akbar carries a rolled parchment scroll tied with a red cord (symbolising mansab orders and troop inspections) in his left hand while his right rests on the hilt of a plain, slightly curved talwar at his waist, and Man Singh carries a long, era-accurate Rajput-Mughal talwar with a gently curved steel blade, traditional disc pommel and simple cross-guard, sheathed in dark brown leather with a small brass chape, hanging from a leather baldric across his torso.

ref_desc: Akbar has an oval face, maroon Mughal jama with emerald sash, cream turban and scroll, while Man Singh has a squarer jaw, saffron Rajput turban, indigo angarkha over mail armour, red sash and a sheathed talwar, all in maroon, indigo, emerald, saffron and cream tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw two full-body anime-style male characters standing side by side as a consistent model sheet: Akbar on the left, compact and athletic with an oval face, wheatish skin, neat pointed beard and thin mustache, wearing a deep maroon, calf-length Mughal jama crossing to the right with subtle golden floral bootis, a narrow emerald sash at his waist over off-white churidar trousers, and soft brown leather mojari shoes; he has dark hair to the nape hidden under a low rounded cream turban with a slim emerald band and a small white feather, minimal jewellery (jade ring, small gold studs), a plain leather kamarband with a simple dagger sheath, and he holds a rolled parchment scroll tied with a red cord in his left hand while his right rests on a plain curved talwar hilt; Man Singh on the right is taller and broad-shouldered with a squarer jaw, slightly deeper complexion, full beard and thicker mustache, a small tilak on his forehead, and intense eyes, his dark hair tied in a tight warrior knot under a bright saffron Rajput turban with a modest gold brocade edge; he wears a knee-length muted indigo cotton angarkha with fine floral print over a visible fitted dull-steel mail-and-plate chest vest with brass rivets, a broad dark-red patka sash at the waist, mustard-yellow churidar trousers, sturdy brown leather riding boots, and simple leather bracers on his forearms; a sheathed gently curved talwar with disc pommel and dark brown leather scabbard hangs from a leather baldric across his torso, all clothing fully covering torsos and legs, and the dominant colours are deep maroon, indigo blue, emerald green, saffron and cream.
